A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ETR/PyETR study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and added material.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of 38 language models on 383 reasoning problems, including correctness, fallacy correlations, and a premise-order intervention.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports individual model-response cases and further correlation summaries.

M1.justification: The problem-generation rules, stopping conditions, thematic conversion, GPT-4.1-mini translation, and PyETR/PySMT assessment remain unchanged. The new appendices document existing components rather than introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 383 problems and 12 thematic settings, with HELM scores for nine models and compute estimates for 19 models as capability proxies. Appendix B enumerates previously described themes; it does not establish expanded evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Table 4 contains the same 38 models in both versions. Models featured in the new case studies already participated in the evaluation; no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The retained evaluation uses the same dataset filtering, correctness and fallacy metrics, 3,000-output-token limit, and 2,400-thinking-token allocation. Fuller prompt wrappers and the theme remapping shown in Appendix E are newly disclosed details, without an explicit revision of the existing protocol.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendices D–E add qualitative error cases involving Claude-3.7-Sonnet, Phi-3-mini, and Gemma-2-9b. These illustrate suppressed alternatives, quantifier errors, and fallacy blocking. The reversal illustration also changes theme, so it does not isolate premise order; the aggregate intervention already existed in v2.

E5.justification: Pearson/Spearman correlations and two-proportion z-tests remain unchanged. The new plots extend the existing 50%, 95%, and 99% confidence-band presentation. Neither version supplies repeated-run or seed information.

E6.justification: The headline correlations and Tables 3–4 are unchanged. Appendix C adds linear HELM results (r=0.671, p=0.0477; Spearman rho=0.650, p=0.0581) and compute Pearson results (r=-0.023, p=0.925), supplementing earlier results. Its claim of significant rank correlations for all proxies conflicts with Figure 2. Appendices D–E also add individual response outcomes.

T1.justification: All 36 formal definitions in Appendix A match across versions after accounting for formatting. The main-text mathematical definitions and fallacy-rate formula are also unchanged; no proof or derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions retain the same claims about capability-associated error composition, uncorrelated overall correctness, premise-order effects, and theory-grounded synthetic evaluation. The noncausal scope was already explicit in v2.

C2.justification: v3 adds post-training methods such as RLHF as a possible explanation for converging reasoning behavior. Appendices D–E also introduce case-specific explanations linking repeated predicates, suppressed alternatives, and invalid existential instantiation to model errors.

D1.justification: Appendix B supplies all 12 themes' preambles, object and predicate inventories, and semantic-coherence requirements, replacing v2's limited description and single example with a substantially fuller input specification. Appendices D–E additionally expose complete prompt wrappers, responses, and their formal translations.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to earlier human-reasoning research and the GPT-only ETR study remain the same. Author-year citations and explicit acknowledgment of overlapping authorship do not substantively change research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized prose edits, numbers the Results and Discussion subsections, adds appendix cross-references, and updates affiliations and acknowledgments. The existing scientific narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the visual presentation through two additional correlation plots and colored, multipart displays of prompts, predictions, and model responses. It also adopts the ICLR layout, reformats the worked prompt, and relocates Table 4 while retaining its contents.

improvement.justification: The complete theme specifications and inspectable model responses improve reproducibility and auditability while preserving the core results. These gains are tempered by Appendix C's erroneous all-proxy significance statement (HELM p=0.0581) and Appendix E's simultaneous theme change, which limits its support for an isolated premise-order effect.
